title: Autopsy and Cipher
premise: Retired detective Beatrix Whitlock, now barely keeping her bookshop afloat, is paid an enormous retainer by a nervous lawyer named Elias Crane to prove that his client, prominent judge Marcus Vale, will not be murdered before his corruption trial begins. When Vale is found dead in a locked study within days, the case Beatrix was hired to prevent becomes the one she must solve — and every detail suggests the killer had access to the original police file of a cold case from her own career. As Beatrix uncovers that Vale's death is revenge for a verdict he buried twenty years ago, she realizes the killer is someone she once trusted, using her own investigative methods against her. In the end, Beatrix chooses justice outside the law: rather than hand the killer to a system already corrupted, she engineers a confession that exposes both the murder and the judicial rot that caused it, then walks away from the wreckage with her identity — and her conscience — intact.
about_author: Noor Blackwood is the pen name of a former forensic archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing unsolved case files before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the gap between what the law knows and what actually happened, from a coastal town whose archives she still visits under false pretenses.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In her failing bookshop, Beatrix counts overdue bills until Elias Crane arrives with a cash retainer and an impossible request: prove Judge Marcus Vale won't be murdered in six weeks. She takes the money out of desperation, telling herself it's easy surveillance work. Emotional beat: pride wrestling with need.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Precautions
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She surveils Vale's fortress-like home and finds him paranoid but unafraid of anyone specific — which frightens her more. A note in Vale's handwriting references 'the Whitlock method,' unsettling her. Emotional beat: creeping recognition that this job chose her, not the reverse.

chapters.title: Dead on Schedule
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Four days early, Vale is found dead in his locked study, ruled a heart attack. Beatrix photographs the scene before police arrive and spots a staged detail only she would notice. Emotional beat: professional dread curdling into personal offense — the killer used her playbook.

chapters.title: What the File Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Pulling her memory of the 2003 Harrow Lane case, she realizes Vale presided over its quiet dismissal. The staging mirrors evidence photos from that file — photos never made public. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; she helped bury something once.

chapters.title: Crane's Nervous Hands
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Crane meets Beatrix, lying badly about why he hired her and when he learned of the threat. His chapter reveals he received an anonymous letter predicting the murder date exactly. Emotional beat: fear of complicity; he suspects his client list contains the killer.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Reviewing her three unofficial 'accident' resolutions, Beatrix finds each connects tangentially to Vale's old chambers. The killer isn't just avenging Harrow Lane — they're auditing her career. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she has been studied like prey.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Vale's widow hires Beatrix privately, revealing his ledger of bribes hidden in a first-edition spine from the shop's own stock — sold to Vale years ago. Emotional beat: vertigo; the corruption ran through her own shelves.

chapters.title: Someone Who Knew My Methods
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She lists everyone trained alongside her: academy classmates, old partners, a brilliant protégé named Ada Renner who vanished after Harrow Lane. Every staged clue is a message in their shared shorthand. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship she thought was dead.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Ada's POV (unrevealed to reader as such). A chilling interlude: the killer prepares the next move, reflecting on justice, files, and a mentor who taught her everything then testified against her. Identity hinted but not confirmed. Emotional beat: righteous certainty shading into obsession.

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The corruption trial proceeds without its defendant, and Beatrix realizes the killer's deadline wasn't the murder — it's the trial's end, when records get sealed forever. Whatever Ada wants destroyed or revealed has a clock on it. Emotional beat: urgency compressing the investigation.

chapters.title: Crane Disappears
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias vanishes after requesting the Harrow Lane archive under a false name. Beatrix searches his office and finds he was blackmailing Vale — motive for murder that doesn't fit Ada's pattern, or does it? Emotional beat: suspicion turning inward on her own client.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Breaking into the courthouse basement archive, Beatrix finds the Harrow Lane file mutilated — pages removed in the exact order she'd have read them. A bookmark left behind is from her bookshop. Emotional beat: violation; the killer has been inside her life for months.

chapters.title: What I Buried
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Flashback woven into present: young Detective Whitlock found evidence exonerating the Harrow Lane accused, and was pressured — by Vale, by her chief — to shelve it. She complied. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud; the theme of corrupted power turns on her too.

chapters.title: The Second Death
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The retired chief who pressured her dies in another staged accident. Beatrix recognizes the escalation: Ada is working down the chain of complicity, and Beatrix's name is at the bottom of it. Emotional beat: terror fused with a grim understanding that she deserves a place on the list.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A note in Ada's cipher arrives at the bookshop, offering a meeting: 'You taught me that files lie when people are afraid. Come be afraid honestly.' Beatrix must decide whether to bring the police — knowing they're compromised. Emotional beat: the choice between lawful procedure and true justice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Meeting at Harrow Lane
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the decaying house where it began, Beatrix confronts Ada — alive, changed, certain. Ada lays out her proof of every death and demands Beatrix help expose the sealed trial records, or become the final name. Emotional beat: two versions of the same wound facing each other across a kitchen table.

chapters.title: Refusal and Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix refuses to help kill again but proposes a trap: use the trial's closing day, when all parties gather, to force public confession — Ada's crimes and the court's corruption together. Ada agrees, because humiliation was always her real goal. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Setting the Cipher
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix plants bait in the reconstructed case file — a fabricated page only the true killer would recognize as false — to confirm Ada's account and flush out a second accomplice inside the courthouse. It works; someone bites. Emotional beat: the detective becoming the author of the trap, using fiction like her bookshop trade.

chapters.title: Closing Arguments
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. On the trial's final day, the accomplice — a clerk who sold sealed records to Vale for years — panics and tries to destroy the archive. Beatrix intercepts; Ada seals the exits. Emotional beat: controlled chaos, every thread pulled taut at once.

chapters.title: Confession in Open Court
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the courtroom, Beatrix forces the clerk's confession and presents Ada's evidence of Vale's bribery and the Harrow Lane cover-up — including her own shelved report. The room turns on the institution itself. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth spoken where lies were law.

chapters.title: The Price of Justice
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ada surrenders to arrest on her own terms, asking only that Beatrix write the true account someday. Beatrix declines to hide her role, giving a statement that ends her chances of ever wearing a badge again. Emotional beat: costly peace; identity rebuilt around honesty rather than authority.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with a new sign and a shelf reserved for books about unsolved things. A young woman leaves a cipher note on the counter — a plea for help, the next case. Beatrix turns the sign to OPEN. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; justice continues outside the law, one reader at a time.
